Calculate Modified Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (M2SFCA) accessibility scores

Source: R/03-spax_e2sfca.R
spax_m2sfca.Rd

Implements the Modified Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (M2SFCA) method (Delamater, 2013). M2SFCA is identical to spax_e2sfca() in step 1, but in step 2 the supply-to-demand ratios are weighted by the squared distance decay. This discounts accessibility in sub-optimally configured systems – where demand and supply are both far apart yet still within the catchment – which standard 2SFCA/E2SFCA cannot distinguish.

Usage

spax_m2sfca(
  demand,
  supply,
  distance,
  decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 30),
  demand_normalize = "identity",
  id_col = NULL,
  supply_cols = NULL,
  indicator_names = NULL,
  snap = FALSE
)

Arguments

demand

SpatRaster representing spatial distribution of demand, or a named list of single-layer SpatRasters, one per demand group (see "Demand groups"). A multi-layer SpatRaster is refused. Demand must be finite and nonnegative (use NA for unknown) unless snap = TRUE, which ignores other cells.

supply

vector, matrix, or data.frame containing supply capacity values

distance

SpatRaster stack of travel times/distances to facilities. With demand groups, either one stack shared by every group or a list of stacks named by the groups (for example one per travel mode); the stacks of all groups must name the same facilities in the same order and have the same geometry (reorder with x[[names(first)]]).

decay_params

List of parameters for decay function (with demand groups, one list shared by every group, or a list of such lists named by the groups):

  • method: "gaussian", "exponential", "power" or "binary", a custom decay function, or a kernel declared with decay_kernel. Weights must be finite where the distance is finite, so power decay needs a positive minimum distance

  • sigma: decay parameter controlling the rate of distance decay

  • Additional parameters passed to custom decay functions

demand_normalize

Character specifying normalization method:

  • "identity": No normalization (original weights)

  • "standard": Weights sum to 1 (prevents demand inflation)

  • "semi": Normalize only when sum > 1 (prevents deflation)

id_col

Character; column name for facility IDs if supply is a data.frame

supply_cols

Character vector; names of supply columns if supply is a data.frame

indicator_names

Character vector; custom names for output accessibility layers

snap

Logical; if TRUE enable fast computation mode (default = FALSE)

Value

A spax object (see spax_e2sfca()); type is "M2SFCA".

Details

Step 1 (unchanged from E2SFCA): \(R_j = S_j / \sum_i P_i W(d_{ij})\).

Step 2 (modified): \(A_i = \sum_j R_j \, W(d_{ij})^2\).

M2SFCA is not a separate engine here: it is the shared FCA recipe with the access-side kernel squared. It is exactly equivalent to compute_access(demand, supply, W, W^2).

Demand groups

Give demand as a named list of single-layer rasters (for example age bands) to let several groups compete for the same facilities. The names are the group IDs: unique, non-empty, not "all" and without a .; all rasters need the same geometry. A multi-layer raster is not taken as groups.

Step 1 sums, over all groups, the demand that reaches each facility, with the demand weights of each group; step 2 gives each group its own accessibility from the shared ratios, with its own weights. The result has one layer per group, and an overall layer <measure>.all: the average of the group scores weighted by the demand of the cell. A group with demand in a cell that its travel cannot reach counts with accessibility 0 in the overall layer; the overall layer is NA where any group's demand is missing or the total demand is 0. With one group the group layer equals the ungrouped result.

decay_params and distance (and selection_params of spax_3sfca() and spax_huff2sfca(), threshold of spax_2sfca()) are each either shared by every group or given per group. An argument is per group when it is a list (for threshold, a named numeric vector) whose names are the group IDs, in any order; names that match only some of the groups are refused. Any other value is shared and checked as for one group. Pass a shared distance as one object, so that it is read once. A plain-function decay builds a whole in-memory weight raster for each group. demand_normalize, indicator_names, id_col, supply_cols and the attractiveness of spax_huff2sfca() are shared.

References

Delamater, P. L. (2013). Spatial accessibility in suboptimally configured health care systems: A modified two-step floating catchment area (M2SFCA) metric. Health & Place, 24, 30-43. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.healthplace.2013.07.012

See also

spax_e2sfca(), spax_2sfca(), compute_access(), calc_decay()

Examples

library(terra)
library(sf)

# Cornwall population grid and travel time to each GP practice
pop_rast <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
travel <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")
gp <- cornwall_gp |> st_drop_geometry()

# M2SFCA with Gaussian decay
result <- spax_m2sfca(
  demand = pop_rast,
  supply = gp,
  distance = travel,
  decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),
  id_col = "practice",
  supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg"
)
result
#> <spax access> M2SFCA, 1 layer on 132 x 271 cells
#> 
#> Spatial Properties:
#> - Resolution: 0.00833333 x 0.00833333
#> - Dimensions: 132 x 271
#> 
#> Measures: 1
#> - gp_fte_extg
#> 
#> Facilities: 55
#> 
#> Parameters:
#> - Decay function: gaussian (sigma = 10)
#> - Demand normalization: identity 

# E2SFCA with the same decay, for comparison
result_e2 <- spax_e2sfca(
  demand = pop_rast,
  supply = gp,
  distance = travel,
  decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),
  id_col = "practice",
  supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg"
)
plot(c(result_e2$accessibility, result$accessibility),
  main = c("E2SFCA", "M2SFCA")
)


# The share of the E2SFCA score that M2SFCA keeps: the average decay weight
# of the practices in reach, low where they are far away
plot(result$accessibility / result_e2$accessibility,
  main = "M2SFCA / E2SFCA"
)
